src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:338-352: _rule_nodes only descends into AnyOfRule/AllOfRule children; its docstring says parent_rule subtrees are deliberately not walked (they read the parent table). So the claim that it yields nodes nested inside a parent_rule is wrong. The second half holds: _catalog_reads (1193-1194) calls _join_pairs(table.name, node) for each yielded node. _join_pairs (rule_sets.py:1150-1164) reads only fields defined on the models. InheritRule (273-284) defines column, parent_table, parent_column. OwnerViaRule (249-256) defines id_column, link_table, link_row_column. ReferencedByRule (293-301) defines id_column, source_table, source_column (optional), source_id_column (optional) and link. ReferencedByLink (287-290) defines table, source_column, target_column. The optional fields are guarded: source_column or "" is used only when link is None (direct variant, validator at 303-314 guarantees source_column set), and source_id_column or "" only when link is set (validator guarantees source_id_column non-None).

_exists (rule_sets.py:564-574) builds exactly one exp.Exists per call. rule_sets.py:934-945 wraps both compiler.compile and prove_compiled_rule in a try with `except _RuleLimitError` before the generic `except Exception`. _RuleLimitError is defined at rule_sets.py:613 and raised only at :628 and :640, both inside _Compiler. prove_compiled_rule (safety/rules_sets.py:445-450) only calls _scoped_body, _generate, _reparse and _shape, and raises ValueError. The safety module imports only CompiledRule, LoadedRuleSets, current_rule_set_selection and refusal_log_fields from sqllens.rule_sets (lines 66-71). It never imports or references _Compiler or _RuleLimitError (grep found no match). So a limit error can only come from compile, and the limit message is used only for real limit failures. Input considered: a rule that fails the re-parse compare, which gives ValueError and goes to the generic branch.

rule_sets.py:875-894: tomllib.loads(text) (line 882) is inside the try; handlers in order are OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError (a ValueError subclass), then RecursionError (line 891). RecursionError derives from RuntimeError, so none of the earlier handlers can catch it and it reaches the new clause. tomllib is a pure-Python recursive-descent parser with no depth guard (nested arrays/inline tables recurse through parse_value), and it does not wrap RecursionError into TOMLDecodeError, so deep nesting surfaces as RecursionError. This is from knowledge of CPython's tomllib; I did not run it.

tests/connectors/test_row_rule_joins_mysql.py:49-67: _TABLES lists all eight tables and _TEARDOWN is a single `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` over them. _SETUP creates rj_src, rj_direct, rj_link, rj_linked, rj_parent and rj_child, which are exactly the tables _document (105-129) names in its rules. rj_tp_parent and rj_tp_child are named only in _typed_document (218-228) and are created only inside test_the_catalog_check_types_each_join_pair (248-249), so the claim is right that the fixture teardown drops tables setup never creates. `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` with a list of tables drops those that exist and only emits a note for missing ones, so the teardown does not error. _SETUP also starts with _TEARDOWN, which clears leftovers from a prior run.

Both queries appear in tests/connectors/test_row_rule_joins_mysql.py:183 and :211, run through _chain(whole_row=True) (test_row_rules_mysql.py:173-185), which wraps RuleSetGuardRunner in WholeRowSelectGuardRunner. whole_row.py:151-156 _is_exempt returns True when the star's parent is exp.Count, so COUNT(*) is exempt, including when it sits inside a scalar subquery. _whole_row_star (135) returns None when every star is exempt, so neither query is refused. Both queries pass through the guard to RuleSetGuardRunner.run_sql (rule_sets.py:874-896), which calls apply_rule_set. _rewrite (583-599) replaces each base table with a filtered derived table: _wrap for tables that have a rule, _derived otherwise. Tables are collected with tree.find_all(exp.Table) (~312), so the table inside the scalar subquery is rewritten too. The counts therefore come from the filtered derived tables and reflect only visible rows. The tests assert len(expected) at line 184 and len(VISIBLE[table]) at line 212. I read the rewrite and guard code but did not run the tests against MySQL.

In _Compiler._node (src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:689-692) AnyOfRule and AllOfRule only call exp.or_/exp.and_ over children with no self._deeper(). parent_rule is compiled at line 714-715 via self._node(node.parent_rule, parent) outside any extra _deeper (the only _deeper there, line 707, is the inherit hop itself). Falsifying input (parent_rule containing an inherit) is rejected at load by _check_row_rules (lines 444-452: parent_rule may hold only _COLUMN_LOCAL kinds), so a parent_rule can never nest an EXISTS; any_of/all_of nested children that are inherit add depth only through their own inherit branch, not via the combinator. Claim holds.

The diamond test builds d16..d00, 17 levels, with each of d16..d01 an any_of of two inherit nodes to the level below. The base slot is d16 (rule_sets.py:657). Each inherit allocates a parent slot (:708) and then applies the parent's own rule (:713), so slots form a full binary tree of 17 levels, 2^17-1 = 131071, base slot included. Depth: MAX_EXISTS_DEPTH=16 (:606); reaching d00 takes 16 inherits, and the check at :639 passes at depth 15, so the depth limit does not trip first. _new_slot raises when _slots >= MAX_SLOTS (64) (:627), so the 65th call fails, and the test asserts 'more than 64 slots' and allocated <= 65. The claim's 131,071 and 65th both match. Absolute-claim input traced: the depth-first walk of the 16-level diamond.

src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:1222-1227 _join_family returns 'integer' for types in VALUE_TYPE_DATA_TYPES['integer'] (181: tinyint..bigint), 'string' for the string set (183), else the type itself. The integer and string sets are disjoint (181 vs 183; the boolean list at 184 equals the integer list and is not a join family), so an integer never maps to the same family as a string. check_catalog 1315 flags a pair when families differ, so types outside both families join only on identical DATA_TYPE: decimal/decimal passes, decimal/bigint mismatches ('decimal' != 'integer'), binary vs varbinary yield different strings and mismatch. Falsifying input (a type in both integer and string lists, or binary/varbinary pairing) does not exist. Docstring at 1242-1247 agrees.

src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:606-609 MAX_EXISTS_DEPTH=16, MAX_SLOTS=64. _new_slot (624-634) raises only when _slots >= 64 before allocating, so the 64th slot is allowed and the 65th fails; the base table takes a slot at line 657 (the filtered table itself). criteria.json is a valid list and carries criterion 2 (this item's text), so it counts; no sibling criterion or disclosed entry was relied on. The test (tests/connectors/test_row_rule_joins_mysql.py:150-157) runs against live MySQL (SQLLENS_TEST_MYSQL_URL, module docstring). The fixture has rj_link, a listed table with row rule flag = 1 (lines 115-117), and rj_linked, a linked referenced_by through it (118-122). Link row (1,12,0) has flag 0 and is the only link row to rj_linked id 3 (tid 12) (lines 62-64). The test asserts 3 is absent from rj_linked, and that rj_src id 1 (the source that link row points to, src_key 1) is still returned. It also asserts the link row itself is hidden. Without the link rule, row 3 would be visible, so the absence is caused by the link's own rule. Implementation: rule_sets.py:730-752 compiles the linked referenced_by as EXISTS over the link table whose condition is self._own_rule(node.link.table, link, link_match) AND the source EXISTS. A link row hidden by its own rule therefore cannot match. The source is judged separately by its own rule, so it stays visible. Trigger split: the only condition that yields a different outcome is node.link is None (line 718), the direct referenced_by form. It is outside the trigger, since the criterion states a listed link table and a linked form, so no input meeting the trigger reaches it.
